settings.rule: forecast for day t+k = flow of day t
mean training-years flow of the target's calendar day, 31-day window

notes: Every model is fitted per basin and per lead on issue days whose target day is in the training years; nothing is refitted on training + validation.
Ridge strength and forest leaf size: one value per input set, the one with the highest mean validation-years NSE over the 12 basins and 3 leads. Test years were never used to choose anything.

Input codes: q = river gauge only, calendar = no live data, w / wq / wf / wqf as in flood.INPUT_LABEL. For wf and wqf the forecast for day t+k gets the actual rain and mean temperature of days t+1..t+k - a perfect weather forecast, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice.

best_by_validation picks by median validation NSE; its test scores are the number to beat. best_by_validation_same_information does the same among the baselines that use no more information than each input set (like-for-like).

Warning scores (pod, far, csi) are pooled over the 12 basins; a warning is a forecast above the basin's training-years 95th percentile. far is NaN where a model gives no warning at all. No warning in the test years at any lead: base_climatology.
high_flow: 5% of training days are above the threshold by construction; the validation and test shares show how wetter or drier later years were.
The forest is random but repeatable (random_state=0); one forest per basin, lead and input set. Only this one seed was run, so the forest's seed-to-seed spread is not known.

The chosen setting is the smallest or largest value of its list for: base_rf_wf, base_rf_wqf (settings holds every value's validation score). A value outside the list might do a little better, so these models may be slightly under-tuned and their scores are, if anything, a little low.
